original_question: Does there exist a twisted geodesic flow with more than one aperiodic energy level?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Remark 4.3 (final sentence), following Example 4.1 and Conjecture 4.2: the open problem asking whether there exists a twisted geodesic flow with more than one aperiodic energy level.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem the paper states in Section 4: it is an existence question about twisted geodesic flows, and the phrase "more than one aperiodic energy level" matches the paper's wording essentially verbatim.
missing_details: A twisted geodesic flow should be defined explicitly as the Hamiltonian flow of the standard metric Hamiltonian H (the kinetic energy) on T^*M with respect to the twisted symplectic form ω = ω0 + π^*σ, where π: T^*M -> M is the bundle projection.
The ambient data M should be specified: M is a compact Riemannian manifold equipped with a closed 2-form σ.
To stay faithful to Section 4, one should include the paper's standing restriction there that σ is nondegenerate, i.e. symplectic.
The phrase "aperiodic energy level" should be unpacked using the paper's earlier definition: an energy value a is aperiodic if the level set {H = a} carries no periodic orbits.
The question concerns periodic orbits of the Hamiltonian flow on the energy level itself, not merely the absence of contractible periodic orbits.
"More than one" should be made explicit as the existence of at least two distinct energy values a1 != a2.
The Hamiltonian in question is specifically the kinetic-energy Hamiltonian, not an arbitrary proper Hamiltonian on a symplectic manifold.
For a fully stand-alone formulation, the levels under discussion should be identified as regular compact energy levels of this kinetic Hamiltonian.
refined_question: Does there exist a compact Riemannian manifold M equipped with a closed nondegenerate 2-form σ such that, for the standard metric Hamiltonian H (the kinetic energy) on the twisted cotangent bundle (T^*M, ω0 + π^*σ), the resulting twisted geodesic flow has at least two distinct regular compact energy levels {H = a1} and {H = a2}, with a1 != a2, each carrying no periodic orbits?
justification: The draft is pointing to the narrow open problem stated at the end of Remark 4.3 in Section 4, not to the broader "transition from low to high energy levels" topic that the introduction explicitly says is omitted. Section 4 first sets up twisted geodesic flows as kinetic-energy Hamiltonian flows on twisted cotangent bundles and says the discussion there is restricted to nondegenerate magnetic forms σ. Example 4.1 then gives the only known twisted geodesic flow with an aperiodic energy level, and Remark 4.3 immediately follows with the exact question of whether there can be more than one such level. Section 2 supplies the paper's formal meaning of "aperiodic" in terms of energy levels carrying no periodic orbits, which is the main hidden definition your draft leaves implicit.
